newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates gain on exporters' buying.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates gain on exporters' buying.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates gained slightly on Thursday, mainly on buying from exporters and dealers said prices would rise further on fears of a delay in the arrival of 1997/98 (July-June) crop.
"Earlier, there were no buyers at around 1,800 rupees (per maund). But demand from exporters has pushed up prices," dealer Shamimul Haq said.

"Exporters are going for low and fine quality stocks and prices will rise further because the arrival of new crop might be delayed," he said, adding that ginners had unsold stocks of about 350,000 bales.
In the kerb market, MNH-93 was traded between 1,900 rupees ($46.92) to 2,250 rupees per maund (37.32 kg).
